results.content:
Title: Preclinical update on regulation of intracranial pressure in relation to idiopathic intracranial hypertension | Fluids and Barriers of the CNS | Springer Nature Link
One of these challenging disorders is idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH), characterized by raised ICP of unknown cause with significant morbidity and limited therapeutic options. This includes cerebrospinal fluid dynamics, molecular mechanisms underlying disturbances in brain fluids leading to elevated ICP, role of obesity in IIH, development of an IIH model and ICP measurements in rodents. In this review, we aim to focus on the preclinical research behind ICP regulation mainly with Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension (IIH) as a disease model. Although it is clear that the activity of ion transporters such as the Na+/K+ ATPase and the Na+-K+-2Cl−-1 cotransporter (NKCC1) are fundamental in CSF secretion at the CP, and are targeted clinically to reduce ICP (Fig. 1), the mechanisms underlying the transport of water at the CP are controversial [5:768–72."), 6:2167.")]. Several studies utilizing small cohorts of IIH patients identified an increased CSF flow rate through the cerebral aqueduct, indicating increased CSF secretion [21:3475–9."),22,23:350–4.")]. Studies utilizing isotope cisternography suggest that IIH patients have increased resistance to CSF drainage, however these findings are not universal across IIH patients and could be confounded by increased venous sinus pressure [24:168–74."),25:851–8."),26:39–50.")]. Furthermore this study identifies that IIH brains have astrogliosis, perhaps explaining previous findings that IIH patients have larger ICP wave forms compared to headache controls, which indicate reduced parenchymal compliance [27, 28:123–8.")]. In one study it was shown that 56% of the IIH patients had hypertension [53:1189–95.")]. Thereby, weight loss has been suggested as effective treatment strategy as it can lower ICP and improves some IIH symptoms [60:4–8."),61,62]. So far this system has only been used in few studies, one in healthy male rats with continuous ICP monitoring for 28 days and two in a TBI model with ICP continuously monitored for 5–6 days [39:576–81."), 41:e0167510."), 90]. One study has shown that amiloride reduced ICP in experimental brain edema in rats [118:416–22.")]. Due to its ability to affect fluid homeostasis in the kidney, we investigated if the GLP-1R agonist, exendin-4, could modulate CSF secretion and reduce ICP in rats [42]. Title: How to integrate IHC biomarkers for more effective clinical development in immuno-oncology - Clinical Trials Arena
# How to integrate IHC biomarkers for more effective clinical development in immuno-oncology. Biomarkers can improve the clinical trial success rate for pharma and biopharma drug developers by allowing for the selection of patients more likely to respond to a potential new therapeutic, by enhancing safety, and by serving as surrogate clinical endpoints. The integration of biomarkers — and the process of choosing from the lengthy number of candidates — into a comprehensive clinical development plan to increase the effectiveness of your clinical trial is always a quandary. ### Histology (IHC) helps us understand biomarker mechanisms in the tumor environment. IHC offers very different information compared with other types of biomarker approaches. Figure 1: Multiplex IHC allows for analysis of a large number of parameters on a single tissue section. Compiling multiplex IHC results with clinical data can allow for the identification of a more targeted biomarker approach for late phase clinical trials. Multiplex IHC allows for the detection of multiple biomarkers (up to eight) on a single tissue section, broadening mechanistic investigations. Harnessing the power of multiplex IHC can expand your biomarker research by allowing for a myriad of analyses, including in-depth immune cell phenotype analysis (e.g., regulatory T cell — CD3+/CD4+/CD25+/FoxP3+) and target localization (e.g., Ligand in relation to a receptor, protein expression on specific cell types). Multiplex IHC is particularly useful in preclinical and early and retrospective clinical studies. Combining the multiplex and clinical data can then be used to identify a more focused biomarker approach that is more applicable in later phase clinical trials. Having had one of the first multi-spectral imaging systems in Europe, Cerba Research has years of multiplex IHC experience and has developed off-the-shelf panels with a number of common immuno-oncology targets. A robust biomarker validation process is crucial for the successful integration of biomarkers into a clinical trial. At Cerba Research, our IHC expert scientific team is flexible in their approach and delivery to providing timely and cost-effective solutions to meet your clinical and commercial objectives. ### Shape your immuno-oncology research with IHC. With special techniques such as multiplex IHC and ISH, tissue biomarkers can yield crucial insights for diagnosis, patient stratification, or mechanistic evaluation.
